place_fields.micro_region: Chandragutti, Soraba taluk, Shivamogga district, Karnataka
place_fields.summary: Chandragutti Gudda Fort is a ruined hilltop fort above the Renukamba cave temple, surrounded by Malnad forest and offering views across the surrounding hills.

planning_attributes.description: An ancient hill fort and pilgrimage site at Chandragutti, with the Renukamba cave temple on the same hill.
planning_attributes.elevation_or_height: about 848 metres above mean sea level
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: Chandragutti was associated with the Kadambas of Banavasi, later the Vijayanagara Empire and Keladi Nayakas. The hill also has the Renukamba temple, associated with the local Renuka-Parashurama legend.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: From Soraba, Chandragutti is about 16 km by road; the fort is reached by climbing the stone steps/path from the temple area.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: The fort is a ruined heritage structure; use only established visitor paths and follow local site instructions.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: The ascent is on a steep, rocky hill path; wear suitable footwear and carry water. The fort is in a wooded area.
planning_attributes.notes: The Renukamba temple lies on the same hill and is a major pilgrimage centre.

place_fields.summary: Yellur Fort, also called Yellurgad or Rajhansgad, is a hilltop fort and former strategic outpost overlooking Belagavi and the surrounding agricultural landscape.

planning_attributes.description: Yellur Fort is a historic hilltop fort near Belagavi, known for its strategic position and panoramic views.
planning_attributes.elevation_or_height: about 2,500 feet (762 metres) above sea level
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The fort was originally associated with the Ratta dynasty and was later renovated in stone by Asad Khan Lari of Bijapur. It served as an outpost/watchtower for Belagavi Fort and was controlled by several dynasties and powers.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: Yellur Fort is about 15 km from Belagavi; visitors can reach the main entrance by road or approach it on foot up the hill.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: Published visitor information lists opening hours of 6:00 AM to 7:00 PM; follow local access instructions at the site.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: The hill has multiple levels and steep sections; use caution on the ascent and around old fort structures and the open well.
planning_attributes.notes: The fort contains a Shiva/Bhootnath temple and an old stepped well; panoramic views extend over Belagavi and nearby villages.

place_fields.micro_region: Annigeri, Navalgund taluk, Dharwad district, Karnataka
place_fields.summary: The Amruteshwara Temple at Annigeri is a 1050 CE Kalyani Chalukya monument built in soapstone, noted for its Dravida articulation, 76 pillars and carved mythological figures.

planning_attributes.description: A historic Hindu temple at Annigeri and an important example of Kalyani Chalukyan architecture.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: Built in 1050 CE, the temple is in the Kalyani Chalukyas style and was a prototype for later, more articulated structures such as the Mahadeva Temple at Itagi.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: Annigeri is connected by road; the Dharwad district administration lists Hubballi Airport as a nearby airport and describes road access via Navalgund taluk. The temple is in Annigeri town.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: Observe temple customs and avoid touching or climbing architectural elements; facilities and access arrangements can vary locally.
planning_attributes.notes: The temple has a roof supported by 76 pillars and carvings of mythological figures on its walls.
